title: Agreement in Bloor v. Falstaff: assigned provisions
summary: The assigned agreement combines the transfer of brewery-related rights, a price including continuing royalties, and a best-efforts provision relevant to promotion and sales.
notes:
Assignment 16 specifically names paragraphs 1, 2(a), and 8(a). Read the asset and proprietary-rights descriptions together with the payment provisions to understand why declining sales could harm the seller even after the transfer. Compare that allocation with the performance evaluated in Bloor.

There is an apparent inconsistency in the supplied reproduction: under “Certain Other Covenants of Buyer,” paragraph 8(a) uses the word “Seller” for the party promising best efforts. That wording is visible on supplement page 59. The Bloor opinion treats the relevant promotional duty as Falstaff’s. The entire contract reproduction is accessible on supplement pages 53–64, while the source buttons here identify the specifically assigned provisions.

textbookImport.basis: Paraphrase of the actual Fall 2026 course supplement. The source retains its own date and legal context; no current-law verification.
